/* All CSS here will be loaded for users of the Timeless skin */

/* =============================================================================
   ANDAH -- Timeless restyle
   =============================================================================
   Flat chrome in place of Timeless's grey surround and blue colour bar, with a
   table of contents in the left rail and an Appearance panel (text size /
   width / colour) at the top of the right, in the manner of Vector 2022.

   What follows the reader down a page and what does not is deliberate. The
   left rail is pinned, and so is the Appearance box; the rest of the right
   rail, which is per-page tools, scrolls away with the page it describes.

   Four of those pieces are not reachable from CSS, because they need elements
   Timeless does not emit. [[MediaWiki:Timeless.js]] creates them:

       #andah-nav-toggle   header hamburger, collapses the site menu
       #andah-toc          the article TOC, lifted into the left rail
       #andah-appearance   the Appearance panel, at the top of the right rail
       #andah-skip         skip links, since the rails come last in the DOM

   Everything they create is styled here. If that page is blanked the layout
   still stands; it just loses those four pieces and falls back to Timeless's
   own inline TOC.

   COLOURS: declared once, as custom properties, in the TOKENS block, and
   overridden wholesale for night mode in section 10. Do not hardcode a colour
   anywhere else in this file -- night mode is an inversion filter, and a
   literal colour outside the token block will not survive it. See section 10.

   SPECIFICITY: Timeless styles the rails at #mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk
   (1,2,0), so a bare .sidebar-chunk rule here silently loses. Rail rules below
   therefore mirror that shape -- both rail IDs spelled out -- and the two new
   panels are addressed through their rail ID as well. That is why the
   selectors are longer than they look like they need to be. Do not shorten
   them.
   ========================================================================== */

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   1. TOKENS
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

:root {
	--a-canvas:        #f8f9fa;  /* page surround, behind every panel */
	--a-surface:       #ffffff;  /* header, article panel, sidebar boxes */
	--a-raised:        #ffffff;  /* popups floating ABOVE a panel */
	--a-sunk:          #f8f9fa;  /* search field, category bar, boxed content */
	--a-thead:         #eaecf0;  /* table header cells, one step above sunk */
	--a-hover:         #eaf1fb;  /* row hover in the rails */
	--a-border:        #dfe3e8;  /* hairlines between panels */
	--a-border-firm:   #c8ccd1;  /* inputs, rules under headings */
	--a-control:       #72777d;  /* the edge of a control you can click */
	--a-text:          #202122;
	--a-text-dim:      #54595d;  /* labels, captions */
	--a-link:          #3366cc;
	--a-link-visited:  #6b4ba1;
	--a-link-new:      #d73333;
	--a-accent:        #3366cc;  /* title rule, selected radio, focus ring */
	--a-radius:        2px;

	/* Set by the Appearance panel; see section 8. */
	--a-text-scale:    1;
	--a-layout-max:    1596px;
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2. PAGE CHROME
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Timeless paints the area outside .ts-inner in #72777d and the gutter behind
   the rails in #eaecf0, which reads as two different greys either side of the
   article. Collapse both onto one near-white canvas. */

body,
#mw-content-container,
#mw-content-container.ts-container {
	background: var( --a-canvas );
	color: var( --a-text );
}

/* The blue strip under the header. It is position: fixed and purely decorative,
   so removing it costs no layout. */
#mw-header-hack,
#mw-header-nav-hack {
	display: none;
}

/* #mw-content-container clears the header AND the strip, at 3.475em. With the
   strip gone, 3.125em would be the header's exact height -- which turned out
   to be too exact: the rails and the article panel then butt straight up
   against the search bar with nothing between them. 3.75em leaves about 10px
   of air, which is what the colour bar used to provide.

   Both the fixed header and this margin only exist above 851px; below it the
   header is in normal flow and the margin would open a real gap. */
@media screen and ( min-width: 851px ) {
	#mw-content-container {
		margin-top: 3.75em;
	}
}

/* Timeless finishes the content column with a 4px green rule above the footer,
   left over from a palette this restyle does not use. */
#mw-content-container {
	border-bottom: 0;
}

/* The footer. Timeless pitches its text near-white, because by default it sits
   on the dark #72777d surround that section 2 just replaced with a near-white
   canvas -- so as written it renders #ffffff on #f4f5f7, which is 1.09:1 and
   invisible. Both modes are affected: at night it lands #000000 on #121212. */
#mw-footer,
#mw-footer-container {
	color: var( --a-text-dim );
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   3. HEADER
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#mw-header-container,
#mw-header-container.ts-container {
	background: var( --a-surface );
	border-bottom: 1px solid var( --a-border );
	box-shadow: none;
}

/* #mw-header is .ts-inner, the centred column the header furniture sits in. It
   anchors the hamburger below, so it has to be a containing block. */
#mw-header {
	position: relative;
}

/* No left padding, so the wordmark centres over the full width of the column
   and therefore over the Navigation box directly beneath it. It used to be
   padded clear of the hamburger, which pushed it 23px right of that centre --
   close enough to look accidental. The hamburger moves out to the column's
   very edge instead; see below. */
#p-logo-text {
	padding-left: 0;
}

/* The wordmark's colour is left to Timeless, which sets #000 at #p-logo-text a.
   That is a more specific selector than anything sensible here, and it happens
   to be the right answer in both modes -- black in day, and the inversion turns
   it white in night. */
#p-banner {
	letter-spacing: 0.01em;
}

#p-banner:hover {
	text-decoration: none;
}

/* Hamburger, built by Timeless.js as
       <button id="andah-nav-toggle"><span></span></button>

   left: 0, which is the outer edge of the centred column -- about 16px left of
   the Navigation box, since normal-flow children start 1em in. That offset is
   deliberate and it is the price of centring the wordmark: the wordmark is
   182px in a 228px box, so once it is centred there is not room for a 32px
   button beside it without the two touching. Putting the button just outside
   the column keeps a clear gap and leaves the wordmark honestly centred. */
#andah-nav-toggle {
	position: absolute;
	top: 0.125rem;
	left: 0;
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	justify-content: center;
	width: 2rem;
	height: 2rem;
	padding: 0;
	border: 1px solid transparent;
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
	background: transparent;
	color: var( --a-text-dim );
	cursor: pointer;
}

#andah-nav-toggle:hover {
	background: var( --a-hover );
	color: var( --a-text );
}

#andah-nav-toggle:focus-visible {
	outline: 2px solid var( --a-accent );
	outline-offset: 1px;
}

/* One bar, plus two more as pseudo-elements. Both are absolutely positioned
   with no offsets, so they resolve to their static position -- the top of the
   middle bar -- and the margins push them 6px either side of it. */
#andah-nav-toggle > span,
#andah-nav-toggle > span::before,
#andah-nav-toggle > span::after {
	display: block;
	width: 1.125rem;
	height: 2px;
	background: currentcolor;
}

#andah-nav-toggle > span::before,
#andah-nav-toggle > span::after {
	position: absolute;
	content: "";
}

#andah-nav-toggle > span::before {
	margin-top: -0.375rem;
}

#andah-nav-toggle > span::after {
	margin-top: 0.375rem;
}

/* Skip links, built by Timeless.js. Hidden until focused, and absolutely
   positioned so that the focused pill cannot reflow anything: in normal flow
   it pushes the whole page down by the height of the header row the moment it
   appears, which is a nasty surprise for the one reader who needs it. */
#andah-skip {
	position: absolute;
	top: 0.125rem;
	left: 2.5rem;
	z-index: 1;
}

#andah-skip a {
	position: absolute;
	width: 1px;
	height: 1px;
	overflow: hidden;
	clip-path: inset( 50% );
	white-space: nowrap;
}

#andah-skip a:focus {
	position: static;
	display: inline-block;
	width: auto;
	height: auto;
	padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem;
	overflow: visible;
	clip-path: none;
	background: var( --a-surface );
	border: 1px solid var( --a-accent );
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
	color: var( --a-link );
	font-size: 0.875rem;
}

/* Search. */
#simpleSearch,
#searchInput {
	background: var( --a-sunk );
	border-color: var( --a-border-firm );
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
}

#simpleSearch:focus-within {
	background: var( --a-surface );
	border-color: var( --a-accent );
	box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var( --a-accent );
}

/* The DarkMode extension's own Dark mode link in the user menu. The Appearance
   panel owns colour now, and two controls that disagree about Automatic would
   be worse than one. Keyed on the class Timeless.js sets once the panel is
   actually on the page, so the link comes back if the script does not run. */
body.andah-has-appearance #pt-darkmode {
	display: none;
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   4. RAILS
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* The globe. The wordmark in the header already identifies the wiki, and the
   logo is the single largest thing in the left rail. */
#p-logo {
	display: none;
}

/* Contribute and Share this, dropped so the left rail carries navigation and
   contents and nothing else.

   Hidden rather than deleted at source: Share this is generated by the
   ShareThis extension and has no wikitext to delete, so one mechanism for both
   keeps the decision in one place. Contribute's four entries are still listed
   in [[MediaWiki:Sidebar]] -- deleting this rule brings them straight back.

   Worth knowing: Help, Community portal, Upload file and Special pages are now
   unreachable from the sidebar. Nothing else in the chrome links to them. */
#p-Contribute,
#p-share-header {
	display: none;
}

/* The box. Timeless gives it a 0.2em bottom border and a drop shadow, which at
   four boxes a column reads as a stack of cards; one hairline all round is
   quieter and lets the canvas do the separating. */
#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk,
#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk {
	margin: 0 0 0.75rem;
	padding: 0.75rem 0.875rem 0.25rem;
	background: var( --a-surface );
	border: 1px solid var( --a-border );
	border-width: 1px;
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
	box-shadow: none;
	line-height: 1.4;
}

/* Timeless keeps its own left/right margin on the first-level rule above; put
   the gutter back so the boxes do not touch the article panel. */
#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk {
	margin-right: 0;
}

#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk {
	margin-left: 0;
}

/* The visible box title. Timeless hides .sidebar-chunk h2 on desktop -- it is
   only there to drive the drawer toggle on narrow screens -- and shows the
   portlet h3 instead, under a 2px rule. Keep that arrangement, hairline it. */
#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk h3,
#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk h3,
#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk label,
#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk label {
	margin: 0 0 0.5rem;
	padding-bottom: 0.375rem;
	border-bottom: 1px solid var( --a-border );
	color: var( --a-text );
	font-size: 0.9375rem;
	font-weight: 600;
}

/* The hide/show control in a box heading, built by Timeless.js. Quiet, set on
   the baseline of the title it sits beside, and pushed to the right edge of
   the box. Only the two boxes this file creates get one. */
#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk h3,
#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk h3 {
	display: flex;
	align-items: baseline;
	justify-content: space-between;
	gap: 0.5rem;
}

.andah-collapse {
	flex: none;
	padding: 0;
	border: 0;
	background: transparent;
	color: var( --a-link );
	font-family: inherit;
	font-size: 0.8125rem;
	font-weight: normal;
	cursor: pointer;
}

.andah-collapse:hover {
	text-decoration: underline;
}

.andah-collapse:focus-visible {
	outline: 2px solid var( --a-accent );
	outline-offset: 1px;
}

/* A collapsed box keeps its title but loses the rule under it, so it reads as
   one closed line rather than an empty frame. */
.mw-portlet.andah-collapsed > h3 {
	margin-bottom: 0;
	padding-bottom: 0;
	border-bottom: 0;
}

#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk .mw-portlet-body,
#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk .mw-portlet-body,
#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk .mw-portlet > div,
#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk .mw-portlet > div {
	margin-bottom: 1rem;
}

#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk li,
#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk li {
	padding: 0;
}

#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk li a,
#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk li a {
	display: block;
	margin: 0 -0.375rem;
	padding: 0.1875rem 0.375rem;
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
	line-height: 1.5;
}

#mw-site-navigation .sidebar-chunk li a:hover,
#mw-related-navigation .sidebar-chunk li a:hover {
	background: var( --a-hover );
	text-decoration: none;
}

/* The three columns hug each other and the group centres.
   Timeless lets the middle column grow into whatever is left, which was fine
   when it grew without limit. Now that the article panel is capped, that slack
   has to go somewhere -- and it was collecting BETWEEN the article and the
   tools rail. Worst on the main page: it has no contents box, so with the site
   menu hidden the whole left rail goes, and its 243px reappeared as a hole in
   the middle of the layout. Centring the row puts any leftover outside the
   columns, as canvas, where it belongs. */
#mw-content-block {
	justify-content: flex-start;
}

/* The article panel takes every pixel the two rails do not, which is what
   Vector does and is the single change that fixes the most here.

   It used to be capped at 48rem + 3.8rem = 828.8px. Three faults came out of
   that one line. The panel was 828.8px inside a 1596px shell, so 311px of
   canvas sat dead, 155px down each side, and the three columns floated in the
   middle instead of reading as one layout. The text column was 766px against
   Wikipedia's 948px. And the Width preference did nothing whatever: releasing
   --a-layout-max widened the shell from 1596px to 1970px while the panel,
   capped, stayed at 828.8px -- measured at both settings, 766px of text either
   way.

   Flexing instead: at the 1596px Standard shell the rails take 243.2 + 212.8,
   leaving a 1140px panel and 1077px of text; Wide releases the shell and the
   panel follows it out. */
#mw-content-wrapper {
	flex: 1 1 auto;
	min-width: 0;
}

/* Rail widths, swapped. Timeless gives the left rail 14em and the right 16em,
   which was fine when the left held five site links -- but it now carries the
   article's section titles, and the wider column carries "Cite this page".
   With sections expanded, 9 of 53 Contents rows on [[1764 FLLA World Cup]]
   wrapped onto two lines while the tool rail sat half empty.

   Only above 1340px, where both rails are columns. The header pieces move with
   them so the wordmark and the search field stay aligned to the columns below;
   the article keeps exactly the width it had, since the two rails simply trade
   30px. */
/* The numbers are Wikipedia's, not ours. Its left sidebar is 324px and its
   reading column 948px, measured at a 1985px window; 20.25rem is that 324px
   and the right rail then takes what is left over so the column lands on 948
   too. Everything still fills the shell, so no canvas is stranded.

   Letting the panel simply take all the slack -- rails at 16em/14em, column at
   1047px -- put 160 characters on a line against Wikipedia's 128. That is a
   fifth more text per line than the thing it is meant to match, and read as
   about a word too wide at each edge, which is exactly what it was.

   In rem rather than em so the rails and the header pieces above them resolve
   against the same 16px root. They are the same widths deliberately: the
   wordmark sits over the left rail and the user menu over the right, and an em
   here would silently drift the moment either font-size changed. */
@media screen and ( min-width: 1340px ) {
	#mw-content-block #mw-site-navigation {
		flex-basis: 20.25rem;
	}

	#mw-content-block #mw-related-navigation {
		flex-basis: 14.4rem;
	}

	#mw-header #p-logo-text {
		min-width: 20.25rem;
		max-width: 20.25rem;
	}

	#mw-header #user-tools {
		min-width: 14.4rem;
	}
}

/* The LEFT rail follows the reader; the right one does not.
   Left holds navigation, contents and Appearance -- things you reach for from
   anywhere in an article, so they stay pinned under the header. Right holds
   Page tools and Wiki tools, which belong to the page as a whole, so they
   scroll away with it rather than taking up a column for the whole descent.

   Timeless already lays #mw-content-block out as a flex row, so the rail is a
   flex item and sticky works on it without further help.

   The offsets are em, not rem, on purpose: Timeless lays the whole page out in
   em against a 15.2px base, so a rem value here drifts. In em the columns keep
   their relationship to the header for a reader who has set a larger default
   font size too.

   No overscroll-behavior. Containing it sounds tidy but traps the wheel: on a
   page whose Contents overflows the rail, a reader with the pointer over the
   rail finds the page stops scrolling once the rail hits its end, and those
   are precisely the pages where the rail matters most. */
#mw-site-navigation {
	position: sticky;
	top: 3.75em;
	align-self: flex-start;
	max-height: calc( 100vh - 4.75em );
	overflow-x: hidden;
	overflow-y: auto;
	scrollbar-width: thin;
}

/* The right rail itself does NOT follow the reader: Page tools and Wiki tools
   belong to the page as a whole, so they scroll away with it rather than
   holding a column for the whole descent. */
#mw-related-navigation {
	position: static;
	max-height: none;
	overflow: visible;
}

/* Appearance is the exception, and is pinned on its own rather than by pinning
   the rail around it. It is a reading control, wanted at any point in an
   article, and it is the only way to reach dark mode now that the extension's
   own menu link is hidden.

   It works by leaning on the rail being a flex item that stretches to the full
   height of the article: that is the tall containing block the box sticks
   inside. It sits LAST, under Page tools and Wiki tools, so those scroll away
   off the top and this pins once it reaches the header, with nothing left
   below to slide behind it. Putting it first instead looks tidier at rest and
   is worse in motion: the two boxes underneath scroll up and disappear behind
   its background, which reads as a rendering fault.

   Only above 1340px, and that limit is real rather than cautious. Below it
   Timeless stops using two columns and stacks both rails into one, where the
   right rail is a few hundred pixels tall instead of ten thousand -- so there
   is nothing to stick inside, and pinning this box there would only fight the
   left rail, which is already pinned in the very same column. In that range it
   sits at the top of the stacked sidebar and scrolls with it. */
@media screen and ( min-width: 1340px ) {
	#mw-related-navigation {
		align-self: stretch;
	}

	#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance {
		position: sticky;
		top: 3.75em;
		z-index: 1;
	}
}

/* Collapsed by the hamburger -- the site menu only, not the whole rail.
   The button is labelled "Hide navigation" and Contents is not navigation: a
   click used to take a 53-row table of contents away with the five site links,
   on exactly the long pages where it is most wanted. The last rule is the
   fallback: on a page with no Contents box there is nothing left in the rail
   worth keeping, so the whole column goes and the article takes the width. */
@media screen and ( min-width: 851px ) {
	html.andah-nav-clientpref-hidden #mw-site-navigation {
		display: block;
	}

	html.andah-nav-clientpref-hidden #mw-site-navigation #site-navigation {
		display: none;
	}

	html.andah-nav-clientpref-hidden body:not( .andah-has-sidebar-toc ) #mw-site-navigation {
		display: none;
	}
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   5. CONTENTS  (the article TOC, lifted into the left rail)
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Timeless.js copies the links out of #toc into #andah-toc and leaves the
   original where it is. Hiding the original here rather than removing it in JS
   keeps the #toc anchor resolvable, and means a failed script degrades to the
   ordinary inline TOC instead of no TOC at all. */

.andah-has-sidebar-toc #mw-content-text .toc,
.andah-has-sidebar-toc #mw-content-text #toc {
	display: none;
}

#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc ul {
	margin: 0;
	padding: 0;
	list-style: none;
}

#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc li {
	margin: 0;
	padding: 0;
}

/* The row: chevron, then link. Section numbers are dropped -- they cost a
   column of digits at this width, and the nesting already carries the depth. */
#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-row {
	display: flex;
	align-items: flex-start;
	gap: 0;
}

#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-row > a {
	flex: 1;
	margin: 0;
	padding: 0.1875rem 0.375rem;
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
	color: var( --a-link );
	font-size: 0.875rem;
	line-height: 1.4;
}

#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-row > a:hover {
	background: var( --a-hover );
	text-decoration: none;
}

/* The section currently under the reader. */
#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-current > a {
	background: var( --a-hover );
	color: var( --a-text );
	font-weight: 600;
}

/* Expand/collapse for a section with children. Drawn as a rotated corner, so
   it costs no image request and animates cleanly. 1.5rem square is the 24px
   minimum target; it was 18 wide, which is a small thing to hit repeatedly. */
#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-toggle {
	flex: none;
	width: 1.5rem;
	height: 1.5rem;
	padding: 0;
	border: 0;
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
	background: transparent;
	color: var( --a-text-dim );
	line-height: 1;
	cursor: pointer;
}

/* It sits 2px from a link that has both a hover and a focus state, and had
   neither of its own. */
#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-toggle:hover {
	background: var( --a-hover );
	color: var( --a-text );
}

#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-toggle:focus-visible {
	outline: 2px solid var( --a-accent );
	outline-offset: 1px;
}

#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-toggle::before {
	display: block;
	width: 0.4375rem;
	height: 0.4375rem;
	margin: 0.125rem auto 0;
	border: solid currentcolor;
	border-width: 0 1.5px 1.5px 0;
	content: "";
	transform: rotate( -45deg );
	transition: transform 100ms ease;
}

#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-toggle[ aria-expanded="true" ]::before {
	margin-top: 0;
	transform: rotate( 45deg );
}

/* A row with no children still needs the chevron's width, or its text will not
   line up with the rows that have one. Must match the toggle's width exactly:
   at 1.125rem against a 1.5rem toggle, leaf links sat 2px left of parent links
   all the way down the column. */
#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-row.andah-toc-leaf {
	padding-left: 1.5rem;
}

#mw-site-navigation #andah-toc .andah-toc-list ul {
	margin-left: 0.75rem;
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   6. APPEARANCE PANEL
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance .andah-pref-group {
	margin: 0 0 0.75rem;
	padding: 0;
	border: 0;
}

#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance .andah-pref-group > legend {
	margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
	padding: 0;
	color: var( --a-text-dim );
	font-size: 0.8125rem;
	font-weight: 600;
}

/* Overriding the rail's own label rule, which is a box title (block, bold,
   ruled off) and not what a radio row wants. */
#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance .andah-pref-option {
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	gap: 0.5rem;
	margin: 0 -0.375rem;
	padding: 0.1875rem 0.375rem;
	border: 0;
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
	color: var( --a-text );
	font-size: 0.875rem;
	font-weight: normal;
	line-height: 1.5;
	cursor: pointer;
}

#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance .andah-pref-option:hover {
	background: var( --a-hover );
}

/* Custom radio: a ring that becomes a ring around a dot by growing its own
   border inwards. Cheaper than a pseudo-element, and it picks the accent
   colour straight out of the token block. */
/* --a-control, not --a-border-firm: an unchecked ring drawn in the hairline
   colour is 1.61:1 against the box by day and 1.98:1 at night, where a control
   boundary wants 3:1, and on a hovered row its white fill sat on the hover
   fill at 1.42:1 -- so the disc lost its edge exactly as the reader aimed. */
#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance input[ type="radio" ] {
	appearance: none;
	-webkit-appearance: none;
	flex: none;
	width: 0.875rem;
	height: 0.875rem;
	margin: 0;
	/* Longhands rather than the border shorthand, for legibility.
	   KNOWN ODDITY: in testing, this ring kept computing #72777d under night
	   mode even though --a-control resolves to #7f7f7f on the element itself,
	   and an inline border-top-color would not move it either, which ought to
	   be impossible. The measurement rig is the likelier culprit than the
	   cascade. It does not matter in practice -- #72777d inverts to #84898f,
	   which is 4.83:1 on the panel against the 3:1 a control boundary needs, so
	   both modes clear the bar either way. Worth another look with real
	   devtools before anyone builds on this token. */
	border-width: 1px;
	border-style: solid;
	border-color: var( --a-control );
	border-radius: 50%;
	background: var( --a-surface );
	cursor: pointer;
	transition: border-width 100ms ease, border-color 100ms ease;
}

#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance input[ type="radio" ]:hover {
	border-color: var( --a-accent );
}

#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance input[ type="radio" ]:checked {
	border-width: 4px;
	border-color: var( --a-accent );
}

#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance input[ type="radio" ]:focus-visible {
	outline: 2px solid var( --a-accent );
	outline-offset: 1px;
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   7. ARTICLE PANEL
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Body typography is left to Timeless, which already sets serif headings under
   a rule. Only the surfaces and the link palette are restated here, so that
   both follow the tokens into night mode. */

#mw-content {
	background: var( --a-surface );
	border: 1px solid var( --a-border );
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
	box-shadow: none;
}

#content.mw-body {
	border-color: var( --a-border );
}

/* The rule under the title is Timeless's one loud piece of colour, at 4px.
   Keep it, thinner.

   1.8rem is 28.8px, which is Wikipedia's h1 exactly, and like Wikipedia's it
   does NOT follow the Text setting: measured there at Small, Standard and
   Large, the title is 28.8px in all three. Section headings do scale, being
   sized in em off the body, so at Large an h2 reaches 30px and edges past the
   title. That happens on Wikipedia too and is left alone here for the same
   reason -- the title is already marked out by the rule beneath it, and a
   heading that grows with the reader's chosen size is worth more than a
   ranking that only holds at one setting.

   A previous version scaled the title to keep it clear of the h2s. At the old
   20px Standard that put it at 38px, a third larger than the reference, which
   is most of why the page read as magnified. */
#firstHeading,
.firstHeading {
	padding-bottom: 0.15em;
	border-bottom: 2px solid var( --a-accent );
	font-size: 1.8rem;
}

#siteSub {
	color: var( --a-text-dim );
}

.mw-body .mw-heading2,
.mw-body h2 {
	border-bottom-color: var( --a-border-firm );
}

/* The heading ladder. Timeless sets h1 to h4 in Linux Libertine at weight 400
   and 30.4 / 27.4 / 24.3 / 21.3px -- a step of 1.11 between levels, which is
   not enough to rank them. On a page like [[1764 FLLA World Cup]] that leaves
   a run of seven h4s sitting 3px below the h3 heading them, all in the same
   face, and a section head that looks almost exactly like the page title once
   you have scrolled past it.

   The serif stays where it earns its keep, on the title and the section heads.
   Below that the headings drop to the body sans, because at these sizes a
   change of face separates levels far more cleanly than another 2px would. */
/* The spacing is Wikipedia's, measured rather than guessed: on an article
   there, an h2 carries 6px of margin either side and sits 24px on a 33px line,
   so a section head reads as attached to the section it opens instead of
   floating in a band of its own. Timeless left 22px above every h2, which is
   what made this feel loose beside Wikipedia. */
#mw-content-text .mw-heading2 {
	margin-top: 0.5em;
	margin-bottom: 0.25em;
	border-bottom-width: 1px;
	font-size: 1.5em;
	line-height: 1.375;
}

#mw-content-text .mw-heading3 {
	margin-top: 0.6em;
	margin-bottom: 0.2em;
	font-size: 1.2em;
}

#mw-content-text .mw-heading4 {
	font-size: 1em;
}

#mw-content-text .mw-heading5,
#mw-content-text .mw-heading6 {
	font-size: 1em;
}

/* Both the wrapper and the heading inside it: MediaWiki 1.45 wraps every
   heading in a .mw-heading div and the skin styles both, so setting only one
   leaves the other still serif. */
#mw-content-text .mw-heading3,
#mw-content-text .mw-heading3 > h3,
#mw-content-text .mw-heading5,
#mw-content-text .mw-heading5 > h5,
#mw-content-text .mw-heading6,
#mw-content-text .mw-heading6 > h6 {
	font-family: inherit;
	font-weight: 600;
}

/* h4 lands at body size, so it needs the extra weight to stay a heading. */
#mw-content-text .mw-heading4,
#mw-content-text .mw-heading4 > h4 {
	font-family: inherit;
	font-weight: 700;
}

/* Links. Two stylesheets already hardcode these -- core, at a:link, and the
   DarkMode extension, at .skin-theme-clientpref-night a:visited and
   .skin-theme-clientpref-night a.new. Both outrank a bare `a` selector, so the
   night-mode variants have to be spelled out here even though the colour they
   resolve to is the same var() in every case; the tokens still do the actual
   theming, this is only about winning the cascade. */
html a:link,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night a:link,
html.client-darkmode a:link {
	color: var( --a-link );
}

html a:visited,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night a:visited,
html.client-darkmode a:visited {
	color: var( --a-link-visited );
}

html a.new:link,
html a.new:visited,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night a.new:link,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night a.new:visited,
html.client-darkmode a.new:link,
html.client-darkmode a.new:visited {
	color: var( --a-link-new );
}

/* Tabs and page actions above the article.

   overflow: hidden is what makes the rule land under the tabs. Every child of
   this box floats, so it collapses to 1px tall and draws its hairline 26px
   ABOVE the tabs it is supposed to underline, leaving a 59px dead band before
   the first paragraph. Containing the floats takes the box to 45.8px and the
   gap to 15.2px. Not display: flow-root, which is the usual answer: it would
   out-rank Timeless's own print rule and drag the whole tab row onto paper. */
#mw-page-header-links {
	overflow: hidden;
	border-bottom: 1px solid var( --a-border );
}

/* The underline belongs to the li. Timeless draws it there and zeroes the
   anchor's border, so colouring the anchor did nothing at all and the tab kept
   its own hardcoded #3366cc -- which matches by day, but at night renders
   #6da0ff against the title rule's #6f9fd8, putting two different blues on the
   page, one of them outside the token system entirely. */
#mw-page-header-links li.selected {
	border-bottom-color: var( --a-accent );
}

#mw-page-header-links li.selected a {
	font-weight: 600;
}

#mw-page-header-links li:hover {
	border-bottom-color: var( --a-control );
}

/* Footer links, for the same reason as the footer text above. */
#mw-footer-container a:link {
	color: var( --a-link );
}

#mw-footer-container a:visited {
	color: var( --a-link-visited );
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   8. APPEARANCE PREFERENCES
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Timeless.js writes one class per preference onto <html> and these rules do
   the rest, so the panel never touches an inline style. */

/* Text. Wikipedia's own ladder, read off en.wikipedia.org rather than guessed:
   14 / 16 / 20px, with Standard at 16px. Scoped to .mw-body-content so it moves
   the article and nothing in the chrome.

   An earlier version of this file ran 18 / 20 / 22px, on the reasoning that
   anything at the reference size had been reported as too small. That reading
   was wrong. What was too small was the amount of text per line, not the
   letters: the column was 766px where Wikipedia's is 948px, so at 20px a line
   here carried 90 characters against Wikipedia's 128. Widening the column is
   the fix, and it is below; the type goes back to the reference size.

   Line height 1.625 matches too: 26px on 16px text. Templates that set their
   own, infoboxes especially, still win inside their own markup. */
html.andah-text-clientpref-small {
	--a-text-scale: 0.875;
}

html.andah-text-clientpref-standard {
	--a-text-scale: 1;
}

html.andah-text-clientpref-large {
	--a-text-scale: 1.25;
}

.mw-body-content {
	font-size: calc( 1rem * var( --a-text-scale ) );
	line-height: 1.625;
}

/* Width. Standard caps the whole layout at 1596px, which is Wikipedia's cap to
   the pixel; Wide releases it and the page runs to the window, again as
   Wikipedia's does. The cap is on the SHELL, not on the prose: everything
   inside -- the article panel, the paragraphs, the floating infobox -- shares
   the panel's edges, so widening the shell widens the reading column with it
   and no band of empty white can open up beside anything.

   This only became true once the panel stopped being capped; see
   #mw-content-wrapper in section 7. Until then Wide moved the shell and
   nothing else, and reported as doing nothing at all -- correctly.

   Measured at a 1985px window: Standard gives a 1596px shell and 1077px of
   text, Wide a 1970px shell and 1451px. Wikipedia at the same window gives 948
   and 1322; ours run wider because our rails are narrower than its sidebars,
   243px and 213px against 324px and 272px. */

html.andah-width-clientpref-standard {
	--a-layout-max: 1596px;
}

html.andah-width-clientpref-wide {
	--a-layout-max: none;
}

#mw-header.ts-inner,
#mw-content-block.ts-inner,
#mw-footer.ts-inner {
	max-width: var( --a-layout-max );
}

/* The infobox does NOT follow the Text setting.
   Common.css sizes it at 88% of its parent, so the Text control used to drag
   it along with the prose. 0.88rem is that same 88%, but resolved against the
   root instead of the parent, so at Standard it is the identical 14.08px --
   which is also Wikipedia's infobox size exactly -- and at Small and Large it
   simply stays there.

   Deliberately excluded from the Text control, on request. Worth knowing if
   accessibility comes up later: a reader who sets Large gets larger prose but
   an infobox that stays where it is. Wikipedia does scale its own, at 0.88em
   of the body; one character here, rem to em, would match that. */
.mw-parser-output .infobox.infobox {
	font-size: 0.88rem;
}

.mw-parser-output > blockquote {
	box-sizing: border-box;
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   9. CATEGORIES
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Timeless puts categories in the right rail, where on a page like [[Dahe]]
   they run to thirty entries and dwarf everything else in the column.

   No JavaScript is involved: Timeless already renders the ordinary #catlinks
   bar under the article and hides it whenever the rail box is present, so this
   is only a swap of which of the two is shown. */

#catlinks-sidebar {
	display: none;
}

/* The 1.9rem side padding is not arbitrary: it matches #mw-content's own
   30.4px, so the chips and the label line up exactly with the article text
   above instead of starting 16.4px to its left. The outline is promoted to the
   firmer border colour as well, because the fill is 1.02:1 against the canvas
   and actually lighter than it, so the box was drawn by nothing at all. */
#content-bottom-stuff #catlinks {
	display: block;
	margin: 1.25rem 0 0;
	padding: 0.625rem 1.9rem;
	background: var( --a-sunk );
	border: 1px solid var( --a-border-firm );
	border-radius: var( --a-radius );
	font-size: 0.875rem;
}

/* "Categories:" is a link to Special:Categories, so left alone it reads as the
   thirty-first category rather than as the label for the other thirty. */
#content-bottom-stuff #catlinks .mw-normal-catlinks > a {
	color: var( --a-text-dim );
	font-weight: 600;
	text-decoration: none;
}

#content-bottom-stuff #catlinks ul {
	display: inline;
	margin: 0;
	padding: 0;
	list-style: none;
}

#content-bottom-stuff #catlinks li {
	display: inline-block;
	margin: 0.125rem 0;
	padding: 0 0.5em;
	border-left: 1px solid var( --a-border );
	line-height: 1.4;
}

#content-bottom-stuff #catlinks li:first-child {
	padding-left: 0;
	border-left: 0;
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   10. NIGHT MODE
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   The DarkMode extension ships no night palette. It applies
   `filter: invert(1) hue-rotate(180deg)` to <html> and then re-inverts media,
   so every colour on the page simply flips.

   That is what section 1 is for. Overriding the tokens here restyles the whole
   skin in one block -- but each value below is authored as its PRE-INVERSE:
   the value the filter consumes, not the value anyone sees. The comment on
   each line is what actually renders.

   Every grey target below is a pure grey, and hue-rotate leaves greys
   untouched, so the arithmetic is just:

       authored = 255 - target

   The link colours are not grey; those were tuned by eye against the rendered
   result. Do not "correct" any of these in the editor -- they are meant to
   look wrong there and right in the browser.

   Base text is NOT left to the filter. Core's #202122 flips to #dddedf, which
   is 12.65:1 on the panel -- fine by the numbers, but it reads as grey rather
   than as text, and it is not even consistent: Common.css sets
   .infobox { color: black }, which flips to pure #ffffff at 17:1, so an
   article and the infobox beside it are two visibly different colours. Both
   are pulled onto one value here, #f0f0f0 at 14.7:1. Off-white rather than
   white on purpose: pure white on a near-black panel haloes at body sizes. */

html.skin-theme-clientpref-night,
html.client-darkmode {
	--a-canvas:       #f4f4f4;  /* renders #0b0b0b */
	--a-surface:      #e3e3e3;  /* renders #1c1c1c */
	/* A step ABOVE surface rather than equal to it. A popup drawn on the
	   surface colour sits on exactly the infobox it is covering, so it
	   reads as a hole punched in the page instead of as something in
	   front of it. Only night needs the lift; in day the border and the
	   shadow do that work on their own. */
	--a-raised:       #d1d1d1;  /* renders #2e2e2e */
	--a-sunk:         #d9d9d9;  /* renders #262626 */
	--a-thead:        #cdcdcd;  /* renders #323232 */
	--a-hover:        #cdcdcd;  /* renders #323232 */
	--a-border:       #c7c7c7;  /* renders #383838 */
	--a-border-firm:  #b3b3b3;  /* renders #4c4c4c */
	--a-control:      #7f7f7f;  /* renders #808080 */
	--a-text:         #0f0f0f;  /* renders #f0f0f0 */
	--a-text-dim:     #6e6e6e;  /* renders #919191 */
	--a-link:         #3c6ca5;  /* renders #6f9fd8 */
	--a-link-visited: #765c9d;  /* renders #a98fd0 */
	--a-link-new:     #bc6363;  /* renders #cf7676 */
	--a-accent:       #3c6ca5;  /* renders #6f9fd8 */
}

/* Making the text token stick. Core pins #202122 on .mw-body and Common.css
   pins black on .infobox, both at one class, so a bare selector loses the tie;
   these are pitched above both. Anything that sets its own colour -- links,
   the dimmed captions, the red links -- is more specific still and unaffected,
   which is the point: only the default inherited colour moves. */
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-body,
html.client-darkmode .mw-body,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-body-content,
html.client-darkmode .mw-body-content,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output,
html.client-darkmode .mw-parser-output {
	color: var( --a-text );
}

/* Infoboxes and wikitables both set a colour of their own -- black in both
   cases, which flips to pure white and leaves them brighter than the article
   they sit in. Pulled onto the same value; cells inherit from the table, so
   only the table itself needs saying. Cells with a colour of their own, such
   as team strips, still keep it. */
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .infobox.infobox,
html.client-darkmode .mw-parser-output .infobox.infobox,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .wikitable.wikitable,
html.client-darkmode .mw-parser-output .wikitable.wikitable {
	color: var( --a-text );
}

/* The search field. The extension pins it to the same flat #ddd as everything
   else, at #simpleSearch under a class on <html>, which outranks the plain ID
   rule in section 3. */
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night #simpleSearch,
html.client-darkmode #simpleSearch,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night #searchInput,
html.client-darkmode #searchInput {
	background-color: var( --a-sunk );
	border-color: var( --a-border-firm );
}

/* Content furniture the templates own: infoboxes, tables, thumbnails, navboxes.
   The extension's own defaults put every one of these on a flat #ddd, which
   collapses them into a single slab with the page behind them.

   The rule these follow is: night mirrors the STRUCTURE of day -- which
   surfaces are tinted relative to which -- and not day's exact deltas. In
   daylight an infobox is #f8f9fa on a #fff panel, a difference of about one
   per cent that the eye reads as "a box". Inverted, a delta that small
   disappears entirely, so the box is given a full step instead. */
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night table,
html.client-darkmode table,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .infobox,
html.client-darkmode .infobox,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .wikitable,
html.client-darkmode .wikitable,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .toc,
html.client-darkmode .toc,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .thumbinner,
html.client-darkmode .thumbinner,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night table.toccolours,
html.client-darkmode table.toccolours {
	background-color: var( --a-sunk );
	border-color: var( --a-border );
}

/* Table header cells, and ONLY table header cells.
   Not .infobox th. Every cell in an infobox -- the title, the section headers
   like Establishment, and the whole left-hand label column -- is transparent
   in daylight, so tinting them here invents a band of colour that exists in
   night mode and nowhere else. A wikitable's th genuinely is tinted (#eaecf0),
   so it genuinely gets one. */
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .wikitable > * > tr > th,
html.client-darkmode .wikitable > * > tr > th {
	background-color: var( --a-thead );
	border-color: var( --a-border );
}

/* Cell borders, both kinds, in both sorts of table.
   Miss any one of these and that side of the line keeps the template's own
   #a2a9b1, which inverts to a warm #5d564e -- so a single horizontal rule ends
   up rendering in two different colours, dark across the label column and
   light across the data column.

   The selectors below are long on purpose. Infobox TemplateStyles are injected
   into the body, AFTER this file, so they win every tie, and the country
   infobox reaches four classes deep:

       .mw-parser-output .ib-country .mergedbottomrow .infobox-label

   Hence .mw-parser-output, and hence .infobox written twice. Repeating a class
   is the ordinary way to buy specificity: it takes these rules to five classes
   and wins outright. Colour only, never width -- the merged-row rules switch
   borders off to join cells vertically, and that structure has to survive.

   !important would be the lazy way to win, and is deliberately not used. It
   would also beat the inline style attributes these templates rely on, and
   flatten borders that templates colour on purpose, such as team strips. */
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .infobox.infobox th,
html.client-darkmode .mw-parser-output .infobox.infobox th,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .infobox.infobox td,
html.client-darkmode .mw-parser-output .infobox.infobox td,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .wikitable.wikitable > * > tr > th,
html.client-darkmode .mw-parser-output .wikitable.wikitable > * > tr > th,
html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .wikitable.wikitable > * > tr > td,
html.client-darkmode .mw-parser-output .wikitable.wikitable > * > tr > td {
	border-color: var( --a-border );
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   11. NARROW SCREENS
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Below 851px the rails stack above the article, where sticky positioning and
   a viewport-height cap would strand them. Between 851 and 1339 they are still
   columns, so Contents can and should be pinned there too. */

/* Contents follows the reader on a laptop. Timeless pins both rails in place
   below 1340px, which meant that on [[1764 FLLA World Cup]] the Contents box
   scrolled out of sight after 887px of a 22,000px page: on screen for 4% of
   the article, while the script went on marking a current section nobody could
   see.

   The z-index and the backgrounds are the price. In this range the two rails
   can pass over one another, so each needs an opaque ground of its own, and
   the right rail is put on top. In practice that means Contents is briefly
   covered while the right rail scrolls past, for roughly the first screen and
   a half, and is then pinned for the rest of the article. */
@media screen and ( min-width: 1100px ) and ( max-width: 1339px ) {
	#mw-site-navigation {
		position: sticky;
		top: 3.75em;
		max-height: calc( 100vh - 4.75em );
		overflow-y: auto;
		background: var( --a-canvas );
		z-index: 2;
	}

	#mw-related-navigation {
		position: relative;
		z-index: 3;
		background: var( --a-canvas );
	}
}

/* 1100px is the real floor for any of this. Below it Timeless stops laying the
   rails out as columns beside the article and stacks them underneath it, where
   sticky positioning and a viewport-height cap do nothing except risk clipping
   a box that is now sitting in normal flow at the foot of the page. */
@media screen and ( max-width: 1099px ) {
	#mw-site-navigation,
	#mw-related-navigation {
		position: static;
		max-height: none;
		overflow: visible;
	}

	/* Once the rails are stacked under the article, a contents box goes with
	   them -- to the very foot of the page, thousands of pixels past the
	   article it indexes, while the inline one it replaced stays hidden. So
	   below 1100px the sidebar version stands down and Timeless's own inline
	   TOC comes back, in the one place a reader will actually look for it. */
	#andah-toc {
		display: none;
	}

	.andah-has-sidebar-toc #mw-content-text .toc,
	.andah-has-sidebar-toc #mw-content-text #toc {
		display: block;
	}

	/* Appearance renders as an ordinary titled block down here rather than as
	   one of Timeless's icon-only drawer buttons, which it has no icon for. It
	   has to stay reachable: this panel is the only colour control on the page
	   once the extension's own menu link is hidden.

	   The !important is answering one. Between 851 and 1099 the skin carries
	   `.sidebar-inner, #p-logo { display: none !important }` to collapse the
	   rails into drawers, and without matching it this panel is not merely
	   collapsed but invisible, with no way to open it. */
	#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance > h2 {
		display: none;
	}

	#mw-related-navigation #andah-appearance .sidebar-inner {
		display: block !important;
		position: static;
	}
}

@media screen and ( max-width: 850px ) {
	/* Timeless drives its own drawer menus at this width off the same rail
	   markup, and a hamburger that hides that markup would fight them. */
	#andah-nav-toggle {
		display: none;
	}

	html.andah-nav-clientpref-hidden #mw-site-navigation,
	html.andah-nav-clientpref-hidden #mw-site-navigation #site-navigation {
		display: block;
	}

	/* The category strip drops back to the narrow gutter the article uses here,
	   or it would indent 30px against a panel that no longer has the room. */
	#content-bottom-stuff #catlinks {
		padding-right: 0.4275rem;
		padding-left: 0.4275rem;
	}

	#p-logo-text {
		padding-left: 0;
	}

	/* The contents and Appearance fallbacks used to live here. They now sit in
	   the 1099px block above, because the thing that makes them necessary --
	   the rails ceasing to be columns -- starts at 1100, not 850. */
}

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   12. PRINT
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

@media print {
	#andah-nav-toggle,
	#andah-toc,
	#andah-appearance {
		display: none;
	}

	#mw-content {
		border: 0;
	}
}
